evidence.quote: The API Key with format `Token token=<API_KEY>`
Use cursor-based pagination to retrieve large result sets.
List users of your PagerDuty account, optionally filtered by a search query.
List audit trail records matching provided query params or default criteria.
Only admins, account owners, or global API tokens on PagerDuty account

assumptions: The users list has no status, suspended or last-active field in the source, so status, user type, last active and created date are left empty. Disabled or deactivated users may not be shown.
The /users endpoint is assumed to return all users on the account when called with an account-level key. The source does not say whether it includes deactivated users.
Pagination for /users assumes offset/limit with a maximum page size of 100. The source lists the parameters and the 'more' and 'total' response fields but not the maximum.

The audit records endpoint is the best available activity signal, but it only records configuration changes made by people, not logins or incident work. Users who only respond to incidents may look inactive.

The audit records endpoint is only available on plans with the 'Audit Trail' feature and to admins, account owners or global API tokens. The source does not name the exact plan, so planRequirement is left empty.
Audit record page size of 100 and the audit_records.read scope for /audit/records are assumptions. The source states the scope for related audit endpoints but not this one.
Some audit actors may be services or integrations rather than users. These will not match a user.
A raw user analytics report (POST /analytics/raw/users) has a last_sign_in_at field, but it needs a request body the source does not describe, so it was not used.
The source says Accept and Content-Type headers are required, but does not give their values, so no extra headers are set. The runtime may need to send PagerDuty's usual JSON Accept header.
A user-level key or OAuth token, not an account-level token, is required for some endpoints. A global account-level REST API key is preferred because it does not depend on one person's account.
OAuth authorization URLs are not in the source, so only the API key method is listed.
Rate limits are not stated in the source, so they are left empty.
